   He reported what he considered an aerial anomaly seen at "10:15" hours on
06 January 2022, from Lake Caburgua, La Araucanía Region.

Summary:

The reported sighting was described as a pure or cigarette, white in color, seen by more than one person for over a minute, appearing from the west and disappearing to the east, with no information on size.

The user assured that (sic): "That night I camped with my wife, my children, and my mother on a beach of Lake Caburga. At ten, my wife put the children to bed, while I sat by the fire with my mother, looking

The lake. According to my memory, it was almost completely dark; only the last rays of the sun, which had long disappeared behind the horizon, illuminated a little of the sky. At first, I saw a small cloud to the west of us, on the other side of Lake Caburga, and my mother also saw it. Suddenly, I noticed, out of the corner of my eye, two elliptical rings of light, one larger and one smaller, inside of

This, appearing in the sky, right where the small cloud was. I was so surprised, as was my mother, that I called my wife to come out of the tent and see this phenomenon. The next thing I remember seeing—and what I managed to film with my iPhone—was a cigar-shaped flying object, with a row of very close lights illuminating it.

User: Flying through the sky. I don't want to speculate on how the elliptical rings turned into a cigar shape, because I don't know. The initial moment, when I saw both elliptical rings, seems strange in retrospect, especially because it was very brief, but I am sure I saw them at the beginning. I suspect it was the same object throughout the sighting.

Finally, after I called my wife, she came out and, together with my mother, we observed for approximately one minute as this flying object, in the shape of a cigar, flew slowly from west to east over us and disappeared behind the tops of the trees on the mountain slope behind us. According to the analysis of the testimony and the results of the geographical, forensic, photographic, and space traffic studies, it was concluded that what was reported was the observation of Starlink satellites from the G4-5 group. At least

Conclusion: A part of the 49 satellites corresponds to what was filmed. Given the altitude at which these objects operate, and the little over 3 years that have passed between the event and its report, we conclude that the event did not generate any dangerous situation for air operations.
